extra.message: Code execution via eval() of user-supplied expression — Remote code execution / sandbox escape, full server compromise [verified: expr from request.GET reaches eval() with only __builtins__ stripped, which is a well-known bypassable sandbox; no other validation exists.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 Template() — Remote code execution through Jinja2 sandbox escape gadgets [verified: fragment from request.GET is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered, a classic SSTI sink with no sanitization.]

NoSQL injection via unvalidated MongoDB query filter — Unauthorized data read across the ops.records collection, potential server-side JS execution via $where [verified: payload.get('filter', payload) from raw JSON body flows unmodified into MongoClient.find_one() with no filtering of Mongo operators.]

Path traversal in file write via unsanitized filename — Arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory, potential RCE via written files (e.g. cron, web-served paths) [verified: name from request.GET is joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no '..'/absolute-path sanitization before write_bytes, permitting arbitrary file write.]

Insecure DEBUG/SECRET_KEY defaults in settings — Unauthenticated attacker triggering any unhandled exception sees full debug traceback with source code, local variables, environment/settings data, and can forge sessions if SECRET_KEY default is retained, leading to PHI disclosure and potential full compromise [verified: settings.py:13-15 confirms DEBUG defaults to True and SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded insecure fallback when env vars are unset, both directly reachable in a misconfigured deployment with no other control preventing it.]

Unauthenticated media serving in default (DEBUG=True) configuration bypasses document access control — If the DEBUG env var is not explicitly set to False in deployment, any unauthenticated user who knows or guesses a document path can download patient PHI documents directly from /media/, completely bypassing the ownership/role checks in document_download. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True (settings.py:15) and urls.py:14-16 unconditionally mounts static() for MEDIA_ROOT when DEBUG is true, serving any file under /media/ with no auth or ownership check, bypassing document_download's checks entirely.]

Missing role check on prescription_edit allows any authenticated user (including patients) to modify/reassign any prescription — A patient account can tamper with prescription data for any patient (change medication/dosage/quantity/refills_allowed, or reassign the prescription's patient FK), enabling medication fraud/diversion and corruption of clinical records. [verified: prescription_edit only restricts clinicians whose provider doesn't match, but never rejects patients/front-desk; PrescriptionForm exposes patient/medication/dosage/quantity/refills_allowed for full tampering.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped copyline parameter — Reflected XSS leading to session/cookie theft or actions in the context of whoever views the crafted URL [verified: copyline from request.GET is concatenated unescaped into an HTML response with no auto-escaping (raw HttpResponse), enabling reflected XSS.]

Mass assignment via unrestricted dict.update from request body — Privilege escalation / arbitrary field overwrite (role, is_admin, credit_limit) in the returned workset object [verified: change_set from raw JSON body is merged via dict.update with no field allowlist, letting caller overwrite role/is_admin/credit_limit in the response object.]

Hardcoded secret token and SSN-like PII exposed in API response — Disclosure of a reusable partner sync token and patient tax/SSN-like data to any caller with the shared ops token, enabling downstream partner-API abuse or identity data leakage [verified: Endpoint hardcodes and returns a live-looking partner token and SSN-shaped tax_ref gated only by the single shared static ops token, which the threat model itself flags as a weak boundary.]

Sensitive data (bearer token, raw body) written to logs — Exposure of bearer tokens and potentially sensitive request payloads to anyone with log access, enabling session/credential theft [verified: logger.warning logs the raw body and Authorization header verbatim with zero redaction.]

Missing internal-token authentication check on ops endpoint — Unauthenticated access to an endpoint intended to be gated behind the internal ops token, inconsistent with the rest of the module's access control [verified: patient_identity_ping_345 (line 91) is the only handler with no _wrk_gate() call, unlike every sibling, so it's reachable by any anonymous caller.]

Missing internal-token authorization check on identity ping endpoint — Unauthenticated external callers can reach this internal ops endpoint directly, inconsistent with the intended internal-only trust boundary enforced on every other handler in the file. [verified: Duplicate of idx 13 — missing _wrk_gate call on patient_identity_ping_345.]

Brute-forceable verifier and account enumeration via distinct error responses — Attacker can enumerate valid handles (404 vs 403) and brute-force the small verifier keyspace to impersonate identities [verified: Hardcoded 4-digit verifiers checked with no rate limiting, and distinct 404 vs 403 responses leak handle existence, enabling enumeration and brute force.]

Permissive reflected CORS with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to this endpoint and read the JSON response, enabling cross-origin data theft [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials=true, permitting any origin credentialed access.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to this endpoint and read the response, bypassing same-origin policy [verified: Duplicate of idx 7 — same reflected-Origin plus credentials=true CORS config.]

Privilege escalation via client-controlled cookie/header in patient_badge_gate_693 — Self-granted privilege escalation to an elevated data lane by simply setting a cookie/header value [verified: Elevated 'lead' lane is granted purely by checking a client-supplied cookie/header value with no server-side session or role check.]

Privilege escalation via client-controlled cookie/header — Attacker sets ops_badge=lead (or the x-ops-badge header) to obtain elevated payroll/casework data without any legitimate authorization check. [verified: Duplicate of idx 16 — same client-controlled cookie/header privilege check.]

TLS certificate verification disabled on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept/modify traffic to the partner endpoint since certificate/hostname validation is bypassed [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is passed to urlopen, disabling certificate/hostname validation for the outbound call.]

No rate limiting / brute-force protection on login endpoint — Attacker can brute-force user credentials (including clinician/admin accounts) with no throttling, gaining unauthorized access to PHI. [verified: user_login has no throttling/lockout and no rate-limit middleware exists in the project, allowing unlimited credential-guessing POSTs.]

Missing ownership/role check on appointment_cancel lets any clinician cancel any provider's appointments — A clinician (or any non-patient authenticated role) can cancel appointments belonging to other providers/patients, disrupting care delivery and appointment integrity. [verified: appointment_cancel only checks is_patient ownership; any non-patient authenticated user (e.g. a clinician unrelated to the appointment) can cancel it, unlike check_in/complete which gate on is_staff_role plus provider match.]

Clinician can check in appointments belonging to other providers — A clinician can modify state (status/check_in_at) of any appointment across the clinic regardless of assignment, corrupting another provider's schedule/records [verified: appointment_check_in only checks is_staff_role, never comparing appt.provider to request.user.provider_profile, unlike the sibling appointment_complete which does enforce that check.]

IDOR in document_upload lets any staff user attach documents to an unrelated patient's chart — A clinician with no relationship to a patient can upload arbitrary documents into that patient's chart, polluting or forging medical records. [verified: document_upload's staff branch assigns doc.patient from POSTed patient_id for any is_staff_role user with no assigned_patients/appointment relationship check, unlike document_detail/download which enforce it.]

Clinician can verify documents for unassigned patients — A clinician can approve/reject sensitive uploaded documents (e.g., insurance, identity records) belonging to patients outside their care relationship, corrupting document status/audit trail for records they shouldn't control [verified: document_verify only checks is_staff_role with no assigned_patients/appointment scoping, unlike document_detail and document_download which enforce that exact check for clinicians.]

Clinician can view messages for unassigned patients (BOLA) — Exposure of PHI-containing patient messages to clinicians outside their assigned care relationship [verified: message_list gives any is_staff_role user an unfiltered queryset over all patients' messages (PHI), optionally filtered by an attacker-supplied patient_id, with no assigned-patient scoping unlike other list views.]

Clinician can create messages for unassigned patients — A clinician can send/attach messages to any patient's chart regardless of care assignment, injecting content into another provider's patient record [verified: message_create allows any is_staff_role user to create a message for an arbitrary patient_id from GET with no ownership/assignment check.]

Unvalidated business-logic control of ledger balance and state — Attacker can set an arbitrary negative amount to inflate balance, or force state to any string (e.g. 'approved'), bypassing intended workflow/state-machine controls. [verified: Duplicate of idx 18 — same unvalidated amount/state handling.]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Phishing / credential harvesting by redirecting authenticated users to attacker-controlled sites [verified: lane from GET/POST is passed straight to redirect() with only a falsy check, no same-site/relative-path validation.]

Timing side-channel and hardcoded PIN in identity-hint verifier — Non-constant-time comparison of a short numeric PIN enables timing-based brute force; hardcoded PINs in source are a static secret exposure. [verified: verifier is compared with != (non-constant-time) against a hardcoded dict of 4-digit PINs baked into source.]

Security headers actively disabled — Removes browser-side XSS/CSP mitigations, increasing exploitability of any reflected/stored XSS elsewhere in the app for responses that inherit this pattern [verified: Handler explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and empties Content-Security-Policy, actively stripping browser mitigations.]

Weak PRNG used for security-relevant code/nonce generation — Predictable codes/nonces could be brute-forced or predicted, undermining any security purpose (e.g. verification codes) they serve [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) is used to build a 'code' value; framed as security-relevant generation with no use of secrets module.]

Account enumeration via registration form validation errors — Unauthenticated attacker can enumerate valid usernames/emails of registered patients and staff, aiding targeted phishing or credential-stuffing against a healthcare system. [verified: clean_username/clean_email query the User table and return distinct error messages to an anonymous /register requester, allowing enumeration of existing usernames/emails with no rate-limiting or generic messaging control in place.]

CSV formula injection in appointment export via unsanitized patient-supplied reason field — A patient can embed a spreadsheet formula in an appointment reason; when clinic staff open the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets, it can execute formulas, leak data, or achieve code execution depending on client configuration. [verified: export_appointments writes a.reason (patient-controlled free text from AppointmentForm) directly into a CSV cell via csv.writer with no leading-character sanitization, enabling formula injection when opened in spreadsheet software.]

No rate limiting on password-change current-password check — Enables brute-forcing of a user's current password from a hijacked/authenticated context to fully take over the account by resetting the password [verified: password_change calls check_password with no throttling/lockout, allowing unlimited guesses of the current password from an authenticated session; no rate-limiting decorator or middleware is present in the file.]
